title: Inference quant & KV quick docket
content:
Quick context:
- Running a targeted microbench and eval pass for a small Llama-style model (7B-ish) under 4-bit QAT-like profiles + KV cache enabled. Goal: understand tail latency regressions when prefix cache hits are low and when sequence length jumps from 32->256.

Hypothesis:
- Primary cause of tail spikes is dequantization overhead + suboptimal kernel path when KV cache is sparse (cache misses cause repeated dequant calls).
- Secondary cause: suboptimal batching heuristics for sudden long sequences (autoscaler/batcher not bumping to different kernel).

What I ran (notes):
1) baseline (FP16) run - single GPU, batch=1, seq=256, prompt prefix 32 tokens cached
   - cmd: ./microbench --model rlhf-7b-fp16 --seq-len 256 --batch 1 --kv-cache-prefix 32 --profile perf.json
   - obs: p50=48ms, p90=85ms, p99=210ms, tokens/s=85

2) quant-4bit (Q4) run - same setup
   - cmd: ./microbench --model rlhf-7b-q4 --seq-len 256 --batch 1 --kv-cache-prefix 32 --quant-profile q4a --profile perf-q4.json
   - obs: p50=40ms, p90=95ms, p99=400ms, tokens/s=110
   - note: p50 improved but p99 doubled -> suspect bad path + lock contention in dequant code

3) stress: drop prefix cache to 0 (cold cache)
   - q4 cold: p50=92ms, p90=320ms, p99=980ms (very bad)
   - fp16 cold: p50=110ms, p90=270ms, p99=520ms
   - interpretation: quant cold-case even worse: dequant overhead + maybe extra memcpy/format conversion on every token loop

Prompt templates I used for evals (short snippets):
- instr-short: "Summarize: {text} -> 1-2 lines"
- instr-long: "Expand and critique the following paragraph: {text} -> 4-6 points"
- code-rewrite: "Refactor this Python function for readability: {code}"

Quick qualitative eval notes (human skim 20 samples):
- Q4 small hallucination increase on token-level punctuation (split tokens), esp in code-rewrite tests (variable names mangled occasionally).
- instr-short largely OK; quality loss visible on longer completions where model now prefers shorter stop tokens.

Microbench commands & helpers used:
- baseline: ./microbench --model {model} --seq-len {L} --batch {B} --profile {out}
- perf check: jq '.metrics.token_latency | {p50, p90, p99}' perf.json
- quick-run wrapper (local): ./run-and-log.sh --model $MODEL --profile out.json --iters 50

Important traces I grabbed: perf-q4.json, kernel-trace-q4.log, nvprof-20260311.out (in /tmp/rhea-traces).

Quick root-cause suspects (things to verify):
- [ ] Dequant path: check if we fallback to non-vectorized dequant when seq-len > 128 (kernel switch heuristic). See PR #842 for kernel selector rules.
- [ ] KV eviction threshold: when prefix < 16 we may be rehydrating KV on every request (investigate trims).
- [ ] Locking in per-thread dequant buffers: look for mutex contention in kernel-trace-q4.log.

Patch/experiment ideas (fast wins):
- A) Force quantized path to use streaming dequant buffer (avoid realloc per token): env EXP_STREAM_DEQUANT=1 run.
- B) Temporary heuristic: for q4, if prefix<64 and seq>128, route to FP16 variant (fall back) to keep p99 bounded. Add logic behind feature flag ff/q4-cold-fallback.
- C) Microbenchmark: try chunked-dequant (dequant 16 tokens at a time) to amortize overhead.

Planned runs (todo list):
- [ ] Run A with EXP_STREAM_DEQUANT on the same workload (50 iterations) — assigned to me (Rhea). Due EOD 2026-03-12.
- [ ] Add ff/q4-cold-fallback behind config and run AB test with 1000 requests (Noah to help on rollout).
- [ ] Reproduce with different model (mistral-like 7B) to rule out architecture-specific kernel selector (Ida).
- [ ] Add microtrace instrumentation to measure per-token dequant time (requires small runtime change; PR draft started).

Open questions / notes to follow up:
- Is the new kernel-selector logic in PR 842 definitely deployed on our GPU pool? I saw mixed kernel versions on traces. (Check s3 artifact tags + docker image hash).
- Does the batcher coalesce short-long sequences badly? Need to inspect batching logs (sre: /infra/logs/batcher/*).
- Consider adding a synthetic TTL for KV entries to avoid frequent rehydration when clients keep jumping seq lengths.

Random working thoughts (notes to self):
- If we fallback q4->fp16 in cold-case, measure cost delta per-token. Might be cheaper overall if p99 drops enough (avoid SLA penalties).
- Could add a quick heuristic at router: if recent kv-hit-rate < 0.2 and seq>128 then prefer fp16-route.

Slack threads and tickets to attach when I make PR:
- slack: https://company.slack.com/archives/C04AMLKQ0/p1678459923000
- jira: JIRA-ML-1192 (investigation)
- PR stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842

Next immediate steps (today):
1) Run EXP_STREAM_DEQUANT (local GPU) x50, collect perf-q4-stream.json (Rhea)
2) Pair with Noah to draft ff/q4-cold-fallback and run a small canary (Noah+Rhea)
3) Ping Ida to spin the mistral-7b variant on infra and run same microbench (Ida)

If I end up not finishing: leave trace files in /tmp/rhea-traces and write a short summary into the JIRA ticket.

-- End of docket (quick, messy; keep iterative)
